title.en: Saddle-node normal form branch and bounded time trace

summary: Explore dx/dt=r-x^2 only on a declared bounded state/time window, linking its equilibrium branch, derivative stability and time trace through r=0.
objective: Show two, one or zero equilibria as r crosses zero and stop numerical playback at the state boundary rather than hiding finite-time escape.
intent_signals: Build the saddle-node normal form with equilibrium branch and linked time trace.
example_prompts: Build the saddle-node normal form with equilibrium branch and linked time trace.
negative_signals: Not a generic nonlinear bifurcation explorer.
not_for: Hopf, pitchfork, transcritical or multi-dimensional systems.
Global claims about an original system away from the local normal form.

entities.name: Equilibrium branch
entities.guidance: Plot r=x^2 with stable x=+sqrt(r) and unstable x=-sqrt(r) for r>0, meeting at (0,0); use line style and arrows, not color alone.

entities.name: One-dimensional phase line
entities.guidance: At selected r show xdot=r-x^2 arrows and exact equilibrium markers.

entities.name: Bounded time trace
entities.guidance: Integrate only for |x|<=Xmax and 0<=t<=Tmax with solver/tolerance disclosed; terminate at boundary and label it.

state_contract.model: Use only xdot=r-x^2 with finite -1<=r<=1, finite |x0|<=Xmax, 1<=Xmax<=20 and 0<Tmax<=100. Equilibria solve x*=±sqrt(r) for r>0 and x*=0 at r=0. Stability is from f_x=-2x. Integrate with an adaptive ODE solver and terminate when |x| reaches Xmax or time reaches Tmax; never wrap or clamp.
state_contract.authority: r, x0, solver state and analytic equilibria own geometry. Camera and arrow scale do not affect stability.
actions: Sweep r through zero and rebuild branch/phase line.
Choose x0, play, pause and scrub stored accepted states.
Toggle analytic equilibrium and derivative labels.

invariants: For r>0 the positive equilibrium has f_x<0 and is locally stable; the negative has f_x>0 and is unstable.
At r=0 the equilibria meet and f_x=0, so do not label linear asymptotic stability from the derivative test.
For r<0 there is no real equilibrium and xdot<0 everywhere.
Every displayed time point lies inside accepted solver output before the first boundary event.
Changing r invalidates prior time trace.
motion_guidance: Playback follows stored solver time; reverse scrub is history, not reverse integration.
Slow display near r=0 may reveal a bottleneck but display speed never changes model time.
creative_affordances: Use a folded metal branch rail and bead trajectory or a plain mathematical board; keep stable/unstable cues redundant.
known_limits: The normal form is local theory and not a calibrated forecast.
Finite solver traces do not prove asymptotic behavior; no integration was run.

claims.statement: MIT OCW notes give dx/dt=r-x^2 as the saddle-node normal form and describe a local equilibrium branch turning so that one side has no critical point and the other has two.
claims.scope: Local one-dimensional saddle-node normal form near the bifurcation; authored bounds and solver policy are separate.

source_refs.locator: PDF pages 6-7, equation (2.10), Remark 6 and Theorem 1

object_craft.structure: Mount the r-x branch plane beside a phase line and narrow time strip with one shared r slider.
object_craft.material: Stable and unstable branches differ by solid/dashed form and arrow direction as well as hue.
object_craft.articulation: The r slider moves a section plane; x0 bead launches a stored bounded trace.

object_craft.structure: In Blender, author only static axes, labeled frames, selection glyphs and low-detail instrument housings at declared units; keep numeric curves, rasters, samples and component lattices out of baked mesh state.
object_craft.material: Use simple glTF-safe material slots and optional baked label atlases with explicit UVs. Export named anchors and static teaching geometry; unsupported procedural nodes, text and compositor marks require baked or runtime replacements.
object_craft.articulation: In Three.js, allocate numeric arrays from the validated input contract, generate dynamic lines/points/instances, bind selections by stable index, and rebuild all linked views atomically on parameter revision or reset.

physical_contract.scope: Bounded numerical dynamics of dx/dt=r-x^2; no physical prediction.
physical_contract.timestep: Adaptive accepted ODE time; display interpolation does not advance the solver.
